transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. How can I help you today?

Well, doc, what brings me in is... I just can't seem to keep my head in the game anymore. Like, I'll start running a safety briefing for the crew, or I'm sitting down trying really hard to review the plans for the day, and within minutes, my mind is just gone. I'm thinking about the concrete pour we messed up last week, or if the drywall guys are going to show up on time, or... actually, speaking of the drywall guys, you wouldn't believe the mess they left at the Miller site. Just plaster dust everywhere, all over the new fixtures. I had to get on the phone with their boss for an hour. But anyway, yeah, I'm off on three other job problems, and I end up missing things in the plans that I know I should have caught. It's getting bad.
Outside of work, do you find it hard to focus or stay on task—like when you're at home trying to read, watch TV, or have a conversation?

Yeah, even at home it's... well, take TV, for example. My wife and I were trying to watch that new crime show, the one set in Chicago? And she's super into it, but ten minutes in, I'm looking at the crown molding in our living room. I put it up myself about five years ago, and I swear the joints are starting to separate near the fireplace. It's driving me nuts. I was actually thinking I need to get up on a ladder this weekend and caulk it, maybe repaint the whole ceiling while I'm at it. Because if I don't do it now, before winter really sets in, the drafts are just going to make it worse. We had a guy at work who ignored a drafty window and ended up with black mold all in his insulation. Nasty stuff. But yeah, what were you asking? Oh, right, focusing. Honestly, I don't really read much anymore, and conversations... I try, I really do, but my wife gets so mad because she'll be telling me about her sister's kids, and I'm just nodding, but I haven't heard a word she said for the last five minutes.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy lately?

Down? Nah, not really. I don't feel hopeless or anything like that. I still like doing my usual stuff, you know? Like, I still love getting out to the garage on weekends and working on my '68 Chevy. Though, man, getting parts for that thing right now is a complete nightmare. I ordered a rebuilt carburetor like three months ago, and the shipping company just lost it somewhere in Ohio. Ohio! How do you lose a forty-pound box in a distribution center? 

I had to call the supplier, and the guy on the phone—I swear he had no idea what day it was—he kept trying to tell me it was delivered. I've got a security camera on my driveway, I know nobody delivered anything. I finally had to dispute the charge on my credit card, which is a whole other headache because my wife usually handles the bills, and she changed the password on our bank app, so I was locked out for two days trying to reset it. The security questions were all messed up, asking for my first pet's name, but I put in 'Buster' and it said it was wrong... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, feeling down. No, I'm not depressed or losing interest in things. Just, you know, frustrated that I can't keep my head straight at work.
Do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks or activities, even when they need to be done, or do you frequently forget everyday things like appointments, chores, or personal responsibilities?

Well, yeah, the forgetting thing is... it's a real problem. Like, just last week I was supposed to pick up my dry cleaning on the way home, right? It was on my way. But I got in the truck and started thinking about the suspension on my Chevy again. I was trying to decide if I should go with poly bushings or stick with rubber, because, you know, the poly ones last forever but they squeak like crazy if you don't grease them right. My buddy Dave put poly bushings on his Mustang, and I swear, every time he goes over a speed bump, it sounds like a dying goose. 

He tried spraying silicone on them, but you really have to pull the whole thing apart and pack it with that sticky marine grease if you want it to shut up. Which is a huge pain when you don't have a lift in your garage. I’ve been thinking about getting one of those mid-rise scissor lifts, actually. They’re not too bad price-wise, and it would save my back. My lower back has been killing me lately, probably from hauling those bags of quick-set cement on Tuesday... 

Wait. Dry cleaning. Right. I completely drove past the place, got all the way home, and my wife was standing in the kitchen asking where my suit was for her cousin's wedding that weekend. I had no idea what she was talking about for a solid ten seconds. So yeah, I forget that kind of stuff all the time. And the focus thing, too, like I said before. It's just... I can't keep it together when I need to.
Do you often act on impulse—like saying things without thinking, making quick decisions you later regret, or jumping into something without fully planning it out?

Yeah, the impulse thing... especially with talking. Like, I'll just cut people off right in the middle of a sentence because I'm so sure I already know where they're going with it, you know? So I just blurt out the answer. But then half the time, I realize I completely missed the actual point because they hadn't gotten to the important part yet. 

It happens on the job site constantly. Just yesterday, one of the sub-contractors, the drywall guy—who, by the way, is always trying to cut corners—he comes up to me and starts talking about the mudding in the master bath on lot 42. And before he can even finish, I'm like, "Yeah, yeah, just use the fast-setting compound, we need it primed by tomorrow." But he was actually trying to tell me the plumbing inspector hadn't signed off on the rough-in yet, so they couldn't even hang the drywall. 

Which is a whole other disaster, because those city inspectors, man, they show up whenever they feel like it. You schedule a window between 8 and noon, and they roll in at 3:30 with a coffee in their hand, looking at you like *you're* the one wasting *their* time. And if they find one little thing—like a nail plate missing on a stud—they fail the whole inspection and you have to wait another three days for them to come back out. It throws the whole schedule off, and then the client is calling me, asking why the closing date is pushed back...

Wait, what was the question? Oh, acting on impulse. Right. Yeah, I definitely jump the gun when people are talking, answer way too fast, and then end up looking like an idiot because I didn't actually listen to the whole thing.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to be moving or doing something, even when you're trying to relax or stay still?

Restless? Nah, not really. I don't feel like I have to be moving or anything. When I'm done for the day and I finally sit down in my recliner, I'm perfectly fine just sitting there. 

Well, I was, until the pull lever on the side snapped off last weekend. Just broke right off in my hand. It’s one of those cheap plastic ones. You’d think for what we paid for that living room set, they’d use actual metal hardware, right? But no, everything is cheap plastic now. It’s exactly like the plumbing we see on the job sites. Used to be all copper, solid stuff. Now it’s all PEX tubing. I mean, PEX is way faster to run, sure, and it doesn't burst as easy if it freezes, which is a lifesaver because the winters here have been crazy. 

We had that cold snap in February and half the neighborhood had frozen pipes. Plumbers were charging triple time just to show up. My neighbor, Gary, his basement flooded completely. Ruined his pool table. It was a really nice one, too, slate top. Getting a wet slate top out of a basement is a total nightmare because it weighs a ton and you can't just tip it on its side without messing up the whole frame... 

Wait. What did you ask me? Something about relaxing? I don't even remember how I got onto Gary's pool table.
When did you first start noticing these kinds of focus and impulse-control issues—was it something you remember having since childhood, or did it start more recently?

Well, it's definitely not a recent thing. I mean, back in elementary school, it was already a whole issue. My teachers were always pulling my parents aside, telling them I couldn't stay in my seat, I was always talking out of turn, losing my homework... and I’d just blow through directions without actually understanding what I was supposed to do. 

I remember this one time in third grade, Mrs. Gable—she was this really strict lady who always wore these bright floral dresses—she handed out this math worksheet. And I just wanted to get it done so I could go play with these new Micro Machines I had in my pocket. You remember those? The tiny little cars? They were the best. I had this one that was a little silver Corvette, and the hood actually opened up. It was so cool. But anyway, my buddy Mike, he had the whole Super Van City playset that folded out into a whole town. We used to set it up on his living room rug, but his mom had this really thick shag carpet, so the cars would always get stuck. 

Shag carpet is making a comeback, you know. I was just talking to a client last week who wanted it in their new build, and I told them, "Look, it looks cool, but trying to keep that clean is a nightmare. The vacuum just eats it." Especially if you have a dog. They have a Golden Retriever, and those dogs shed like crazy. You need one of those heavy-duty Dyson vacuums for that, the ones with the ball. I bought my wife one of those a few years ago for Christmas. Probably not the most romantic gift, but hey, it works great. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, Mrs. Gable and the math worksheet. Yeah, I rushed through the whole thing, got every single answer wrong because I didn't read the instructions, and she made me sit inside during recess to do it again. So, yeah, it’s been happening since I was a kid.
